restrictions: Complete fixed-IV SHA3-256 sponge (rate 1088, capacity 512, suffix 0x06, pad10*1), prefix rounds 0 through 4, all 256 output bits; every message is exactly 64 bytes (one block).

Generic birthday search over N = 2^128 messages in 2^96 groups of 2^32: group g has a fresh uniform 64-byte prefix P_g (two random 256-bit words) and message m(g,z) is P_g with LE32(z) XORed into bytes 0..3 and 40..43 (low halves of lanes 0 and 5, one theta column). Groups are processed in batches of 256 (one group per bit position of every 256-bit word, bitsliced), z = gray(t) for t = 0..2^32-1.

Each z-step of a batch (256 messages) is an exact counted straight-line word-RAM program of at most 48,451 operations on its worst path: Gray update of the round-2 theta output A2 on 62 words, bitsliced rounds 2-4 with theta parities/D words formed in the same pass (rotations are address renamings, never executed; round 4 stores only the 5 diagonal lanes), the digest-only part of round 5 (the last round), a 256x256 delta-swap bit transpose to per-message 256-bit keys, one Briggs-Torczon sparse-set step per message on the top 140 key bits, and loop control (ctz dispatch by a branch tree, no indirect jump). The claimed charge adds one address addition for each of its 14,360 direct-address loads/stores and one immediate move for each of its 12 ALU immediates (62,823 per z-step, 245.40 per message) and charges 248 operations = 248/1355 units per message, including per-batch setup (< 2^20 operations per 2^40 messages).

Classical probabilistic 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5 with 64 registers as our stated assumption (the program uses at most 48; table bases and constants are held in registers): one five-round permutation costs 1 unit; every load, store, address addition, logic operation, shift, comparison, conditional branch, immediate move and random word costs 1/1355. Without the extra charges the same program gives 192 operations per message and 125.181; also charging every shift amount gives 258 and 125.608 (proof Section 9).

Time bound T <= 2^128*248/1355 + 3 < 2^125.55012 holds in every run (no restarts; the run halts at the first full-key match after at most 2 verification permutations). The success probability 0.39 (model value 0.39334) relies on the declared heuristic H1; output correctness and all resource bounds are unconditional.

The scalar last-round early abort was published on this track by ercumentyildirim (4c969300); our bitsliced digest-only last round is the same observation. This is the five-round port of our sha3-256-r6 package (ticket 377eebd5). None of them has reviewed this package; the combination, the SHA3-specific lemmas and the counted program, and any errors in them, are ours.

No cryptanalytic weakness of SHA3 is claimed: this is a constant-factor improvement of a full-digest birthday search under the operation-level cost model. Memory is about 2^145 bytes (reported only, not a Pareto improvement).

heuristics.statement: For the failure events F1 and F2 (Section 7), the 2^128 keys of the grouped message set {m(g, z)} (independent uniform prefixes P_g, all z in {0,1}^32, processed in any fixed order chosen independently of the digests, in particular the order of Section 2: batch by batch, t = 0..2^32-1 with z = gray(t), slots p = r + 32i for r = 0..31 and i = 0..7) behave like N independent uniform 256-bit values, i.e. Pr[F1] <= exp(-N(N-1)/2^257) and Pr[F2] <= N^3/6 * 2^-396.
heuristics.scope: Only the success probability (Section 7) uses H1. Evaluator exactness, verification of every output, and all time, memory and preprocessing bounds are unconditional. Cross-group pairs (all but a 2^-96 fraction of pairs) provably collide with probability >= 2^-256 each (Cauchy-Schwarz over the uniform prefixes), so the expected number of colliding pairs is at least (1-2^-96)/2 without H1; H1 is needed for the second-moment behaviour behind Pr[F1] and for F2. Bitslicing and batching change neither the message set nor any digest value; they fix only the processing order, which depends on (batch, t, slot) and never on digests.
heuristics.extrapolation: Tested at scale only: four organizer-executed scaled analogues with N_t = 2^9 messages and an 18-bit digest mask (N_t^2/2^18 = 1 = N^2/2^256), all computing digests with the bitsliced grouped evaluator itself: 256 groups x 2 (a full batch; groups far outnumber group size, as at full scale), 16 groups x 32, a single group of 512 (strongest within-group structure) and 4 groups x 128 with the varying z bits at 25..31. Every organizer trial also checks 5 full 256-bit keys (the first 4 in processing order and the last, at a Gray-updated z) against an independent direct sponge and checks the 62-word support of each Gray coefficient column. Local runs (all reported): an organizer-runner replay at 256 trials per layout (spread layout at -2.4 sd), two batches of 8,192 trials per layout (all within +-2.5 sd per batch, spread pooled +0.4), and a direct check of 8,388,608 within-group one-bit-z pairs (masked matches 34/35/37/33 vs 32 expected; mean digest-difference weight 128.00). The claim extrapolates uniform-model behaviour to N = 2^128 and the full 256-bit key.
heuristics.limitations: H1 is not proved. Within a group the round-2 theta output A2 is exactly affine in z (Lemma 2), a stronger structure than in a generic search; only four nonlinear chi layers (rounds 2-5) follow, but masked low-width experiments cannot exclude a structural effect that appears only at full width. Organizer seeds are public. The scaled experiments resolve the success frequency only to about +-0.03 at 256 trials. The 0.0033 allowance between the model value 0.39334 and the claimed 0.39 is not statistically certified. Within a group the digest has algebraic degree at most 16 in z (affine A2, then four chi layers), so it sums to zero over every 17-dimensional affine subspace of z (participant-side check: two random 17-cubes sum to zero, a 15- and a 16-cube do not); no experiment varies more than 9 z bits. This concerns only within-group pairs (a 2^-96 fraction); a relation between two whole groups would need P_g XOR P_g' in the 32-dimensional z-insertion span (probability 2^-480 per pair of groups), and we see no route from it to clustering of cross-group collisions, but H1 assumes there is none.
